questions.q: What are the three attributes every PyTorch tensor carries?
options: name, shape, and owner
shape, dtype, and device
rank, size, and color
index, value, and label
questions.explain: Every tensor has a shape (its dimensions), a dtype (element type like float32), and a device (cpu or cuda). Mismatches among these cause most PyTorch runtime errors.

questions.q: What is the key difference between torch.view() and torch.reshape()?
options: view() changes values, reshape() does not
reshape() only works on GPU tensors
view() requires the tensor to be contiguous in memory; reshape() falls back to copying if needed
There is no difference; they are aliases
questions.explain: view() requires contiguous memory and will error otherwise. reshape() behaves the same when possible but copies the data when the tensor isn't contiguous, making it the safer default.

questions.q: Given x with shape (3, 4) and w with shape (4, 5), what does x @ w produce?
options: A tensor of shape (3, 5), the matrix product
An error, because the shapes don't match
A tensor of shape (4, 4), elementwise multiplied
A tensor of shape (3, 4), unchanged
questions.explain: Matrix multiplication follows the rule (m, n) @ (n, p) -> (m, p). Here that's (3, 4) @ (4, 5) -> (3, 5).

questions.q: Two tensors have shapes (3, 4) and (4,). Can they be combined with the + operator, and why?
options: No, elementwise operators never allow different shapes
Yes, because broadcasting treats the (4,) tensor as compatible with the last dimension of (3, 4) and repeats it across rows
No, only torch.matmul supports shape differences
Yes, but only after converting both to NumPy arrays
questions.explain: Broadcasting compares shapes from the right; a trailing dimension of 4 matches 4, and the missing leading dimension is treated as 1 and expanded to 3, so the (4,) tensor is broadcast across each row.

Creates a boolean mask of where a equals zero
questions.explain: The _like family (zeros_like, ones_like, randn_like) creates a new tensor matching another tensor's shape and dtype, saving you from retyping the shape.
